slides.title: Root Types: Tap and Fibrous 🌱
slides.text: Plants have roots to anchor them and absorb water! A tap root has one thick main root with side branches (like carrot and mustard). A fibrous root has many thin equal roots spreading out (like grass and onion).
slides.spoken: Plants have roots to anchor them and absorb water! A tap root has one thick main root with side branches like carrot. A fibrous root has many thin equal roots like grass!

slides.title: Photosynthesis: The Leaf's Kitchen ☀️
slides.text: Green leaves make food using sunlight! Chlorophyll (green pigment) traps sunlight. The leaf mixes water from roots and carbon dioxide from air to make starch (food) and releases oxygen!
slides.spoken: Green leaves make food using sunlight! Chlorophyll traps sunlight. The leaf mixes water and carbon dioxide to make starch food and releases oxygen!

slides.title: Transpiration: Leaf Cooling 💧
slides.text: Leaves lose extra water as water vapour through tiny pores called stomata! This transpiration keeps the plant cool on hot days and helps pull fresh water up from the roots.
slides.spoken: Leaves lose extra water as water vapour through tiny pores called stomata! This transpiration keeps the plant cool and pulls water up from the roots.

slides.title: Composition of Air 🌬️
slides.text: Air is a mixture of gases! Nitrogen makes up about 78 percent of air. Oxygen makes up about 21 percent. Carbon dioxide is about 0.04 percent. Air also has water vapour and dust.
slides.spoken: Air is a mixture of gases! Nitrogen makes up about 78 percent of air. Oxygen makes up about 21 percent. Carbon dioxide is a tiny bit at 0.04 percent.

slides.title: Breathing and Burning 🔥
slides.text: Both breathing and burning need oxygen! Breathing takes in oxygen for living cells. Burning needs oxygen to keep a fire or candle flame going. Without oxygen, a candle goes out!
slides.spoken: Both breathing and burning need oxygen! Breathing takes in oxygen for living cells. Burning needs oxygen to keep a candle flame going. Without oxygen, a fire goes out!

challenges.question: What is PHOTOSYNTHESIS?
challenges.answer: The process by which green leaves make food using sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide
options: The process by which green leaves make food using sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide
The process by which plants drink water from soil
The process by which plants breathe in oxygen
challenges.hint: Think about what a green leaf does in the sun with water and air!
challenges.misconception: Photosynthesis is NOT just drinking water or breathing! It is the special food-making process where green leaves use sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide to make starch and oxygen!

challenges.question: Which green substance in leaves traps sunlight for photosynthesis?
options: Chlorophyll
Starch
Iodine
challenges.hint: It is the green pigment inside leaves that gives them their green colour!
challenges.misconception: The substance is chlorophyll, NOT starch or iodine! Starch is the food made, and iodine is the testing liquid used in the laboratory!

options: Starch
Chlorophyll

challenges.question: Drag each item into the correct group: Raw materials vs Products of photosynthesis!
challenges.hint: Raw materials are what the leaf takes in (sunlight, water, carbon dioxide). Products are what it makes (starch, oxygen)!
challenges.misconception: Remember: sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide go INTO the leaf (raw materials), while starch and oxygen come OUT (products)!

challenges.question: How do we TEST a leaf for the presence of starch?
challenges.answer: Iodine test — turns blue-black if starch is present
options: Iodine test — turns blue-black if starch is present
Boil the leaf in water and see if it turns green
Smell the leaf to check for sweet food
challenges.hint: We drop a brownish testing liquid onto the leaf. What colour does it turn if starch is there?
challenges.misconception: We use the iodine test! When iodine touches starch, it turns a deep blue-black colour. Boiling alone does not test for starch!

challenges.question: Drag each plant part to its root system type: Tap root or Fibrous root!
challenges.hint: Tap roots have one main thick root (carrot, mustard). Fibrous roots have many equal thin roots (grass, onion)!
challenges.misconception: Thickness alone is not enough! A tap root has ONE main thick root with side branches (carrot, mustard). A fibrous root has MANY thin equal roots from the stem base (grass, onion)!

challenges.question: Air is a mixture of gases. Which gas makes up the LARGEST part of air?
options: Nitrogen (about 78%)
Oxygen (about 21%)
Carbon dioxide (about 0.04%)
challenges.hint: It makes up almost 78 parts out of 100 in the atmosphere, but we do not use it for breathing!
challenges.misconception: Nitrogen is the LARGEST part at 78%! Oxygen is only 21%. Many students mistakenly think air is mostly oxygen because we need oxygen to survive.

options: Oxygen (about 21%)
Nitrogen (about 78%)

challenges.question: Drag each gas to its correct percentage in air!
challenges.hint: Nitrogen is 78%, Oxygen is 21%, Carbon dioxide is 0.04%!
challenges.misconception: Check the exact numbers: Nitrogen = 78%, Oxygen = 21%, Carbon dioxide = 0.04%! Do not mix up nitrogen and oxygen percentages!

easierVariant.hint: Take it slow. Nitrogen is 78%, Oxygen is 21%, Carbon dioxide is 0.04%!

challenges.question: Drag each statement to Breathing or Burning!
challenges.hint: Breathing happens in living bodies and is slow. Burning happens outside with flames and produces heat!
challenges.misconception: Breathing and burning both use oxygen, but breathing is slow and inside living bodies, while burning is fast, outside, and produces heat and light!
